title: TrueNorth character
description: One playable or non-playable character, `content/characters/<id>.json`. It describes the rig contract - artboard, state machine, inputs, skin slots - in vocabulary both backends of ICharacterRenderer honour, so a character never knows whether it was drawn by Rive or by a sprite atlas.

name.description: Display name, carried inline (ADR-0010). A Mountie is named by role, never by a real person or a force.

artboard.description: Rive artboard name, or the atlas namespace the sprite fallback uses. Identical in both.

stateMachine.description: Rive state machine name; the sprite fallback derives its animation selection from the same inputs.

inputs.description: State-machine inputs the rig must expose. Slice 1 task 1.11's contract test loads the .riv and asserts each of these exists, which is only possible because they are declared as data here.

slots.description: Every skin slot this character offers, with its options and its default. Slot and option names are identical in Rive and in the sprite atlas (CLAUDE.md, Characters); that identity is what makes the fallback a swap rather than a port. Declared as data so the character creator renders itself from the document instead of from a hardcoded list - adding a slot is content, not an engine change.

indigenous.description: Is this character depicted as Indigenous? Required and never inferred, so the judgement is recorded rather than defaulted - the same shape as factClaim.factual and for the same reason. False is a real answer: docs/content-review.md 3.3 gives exactly two outcomes for a depiction with no nameable nation, and the second is a character who carries no cultural marker at all and about whom the game asserts nothing.

nation.description: The nation depicted. Required whenever `indigenous` is true, and forbidden otherwise - naming a nation for a character not depicted as Indigenous is a claim nobody meant to make.

nationSource.description: Where the name in `nation` was copied from, and the verifier's check of it.

communityReview.description: Whether the nation depicted has been asked. An agent may write status "not-sought" and nothing else (docs/content-review.md 1).

allOf.$comment: docs/content-review.md 3: a character depicted as Indigenous names one nation, cites it, and records whether the nation has been asked. A character not so depicted carries none of the three, so an unused nation field cannot sit in a file looking like a claim. Only property names this object already declares appear here (ADR-0007).

characterSlot.title: Character slot
characterSlot.description: One runtime-swappable slot: skin tone, hair, coat. `playerSelectable` is what the character creator shows; an NPC's costume slots are not selectable and are never offered to a player.

name.description: Slot name, identical in the Rive artboard and in the atlas frame prefixes.

labelKey.description: Localiser key naming the slot in the creator, e.g. creator.slot.hair. A key, not inline text: it is UI vocabulary reused by every character (ADR-0010).

fallback.description: Option id used when nothing has been chosen: an NPC document, and save recovery when a saved option id no longer exists. NOT a pre-selection. It was called `default` for one day and that name was the whole of a real conflict with assets/style/art-bible.md 8, which says no skin tone is the default - a field named `default` reads as "show this one chosen", and a pre-chosen tone is a statement about who the standard player is, made in a data file where nobody reads it. The creator randomises uniformly over every option on open (docs/content-review.md 8.3); that is UI behaviour, checked by task 1.15's seeded-draw test, not by this schema. Must be one of options[].id; validate-content cross-checks it.

characterSkinOption.title: Character skin option
characterSkinOption.description: One choice inside a slot. Every option has a name shown as text: colour is never the only signal (CLAUDE.md, Accessibility).

labelKey.description: Localiser key naming the option, e.g. creator.hair.curly.

characterInput.title: Character input
characterInput.description: One state-machine input. `kind` is what ICharacterRenderer's setBool, setNumber and fire address.
